content.text: I have inspected every MFN-flavoured provision. All run against the Terminal Parties (counterparties), not against us.

input.quote: 15.2 The facilities provided pursuant to Subparagraph 15.1 shall be suitable for extending capacity in the APCN 2 of all payload types as defined in Subparagraph 15.3 and shall be furnished and maintained on terms and conditions which shall be no less favorable than those granted to another Carrier for transmission facilities of similar type and quantity transiting the location involved.
input.rationale: The only "no less favorable" / non-discrimination mechanics in the Agreement bind the Terminal Parties, and Teleglobe USA Inc. is not one of them (Subparagraph (s): "The Terminal Parties are China Telecom, CWHKTI, Chunghwa Telecom, KDD, Korea Telecom, NTT Com, PLDT, SingTel, and Telekom Malaysia."). Subparagraph 15.1-15.2 obliges the Terminal Parties to furnish transiting facilities to us on terms no less favourable than those granted to any other Carrier, and Subparagraphs 17.1-17.4 require reasonable, non-discriminatory Direct Access arrangements from the Terminal Parties. Both therefore run in our favour as a non-Terminal Party and capacity owner, and the playbook expressly welcomes MFN pricing in the Customer's favour. Conversely, nothing obliges us to extend our best terms to any other Party: Subparagraphs 12.20 and 12.21 make the "terms and conditions including pricing of such private IRU sales ... bilateral matters between granting Party and purchaser", and Subparagraph 12.22 lets any Party make its Allocated Capacity available "on any commercial basis without any restrictions". The preferred position (no Customer MFN obligation benefiting the counterparty) is met, so no redline is proposed.

mappings.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
